clue.text: Temptress acclaimed after capturing gentleman's heart back

indicators.note: back at the end of the clue says the whole assembled piece is read in the opposite direction
capturing means the word for acclaimed holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: acclaimed means hailed, cheered on

indicators.note: the heart of gentleman is its central letter, the fifth of nine

explanation.surface: A seductive woman is applauded after winning over a man's affections again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' puts L (the heart of gentleman) inside HAILED, giving HALILED; 'back' then reverses it all.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Delilah seduced Samson and betrayed him, so her name stands for any temptress.

clue.text: Human resources needed by a small uninhabited island

parts.note: the human resources of a firm are its staff, its workforce

explanation.surface: A personnel department is required on a tiny deserted isle.
explanation.walkthrough: Staffa is a small uninhabited island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland, home of Fingal's Cave.
explanation.definitionFit: A proper-name example: this Hebridean islet off Mull has no permanent residents.

clue.text: Observation from absolute expert making case for Newton

parts.note: absolute, as in an absolute fool, means utter

indicators.note: the word for expert forms a case, a surrounding shell, for the next piece

parts.note: an expert is an ace
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: A remark from a total authority defending the great physicist Isaac Newton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making case for' puts N inside ACE, giving ANCE after UTTER. Newton looks like the scientist, but it is the unit, abbreviated N.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an observation is a remark, something spoken aloud, which is an utterance.

clue.text: Type of exceptional talent I wasted

indicators.note: wasted here means lost or thrown away, so the letter I is removed

parts.note: an exceptional talent is a genius

explanation.surface: A kind of brilliant gift that the speaker has squandered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' takes the I out of GENIUS.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a genus is a rank of classification, so it means a type or kind.

clue.text: Dreamy and low state of Manhattan

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
Manhattan is in New York state, abbreviated NY

explanation.surface: A wistful, downbeat mood in the city of Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like a mood adjective beside 'Dreamy', but it is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone moony is dreamy and listless, lost in idle thoughts.

clue.text: Dear old wife and son with writer — this writer's?

parts.note: a former wife is an ex
a pen is a writing instrument
this writer is the setter, I; 'writer's' read as 'writer has' gives I've

explanation.surface: A costly divorce settlement: former wife, son, and an author ask whether the setter will pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this writer's' is the setter saying 'I have', contracted to I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something dear costs a lot of money, as in 'petrol is dear'.

clue.text: Do without leader after beginning of joint meeting

indicators.note: after means the decapitated word comes after the opening letter of joint
the beginning of joint is its first letter
without leader means the first letter is removed from the word for do

parts.note: a do is a party or function

explanation.surface: Manage without a chief once a shared session has started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' reads as a verb, but it is the noun for a party, FUNCTION, which loses its F before being put after J.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a junction is a point where roads or lines meet, a meeting place.

clue.text: Amuse some, but not second time

indicators.note: the letter for time is put in, but not the letter for second, which it replaces

parts.note: divers is an old word meaning several or some

explanation.surface: Entertain a few people, though not a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: DIVERS (archaic 'several') swaps its S (second) for T (time).
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to divert people is to entertain or amuse them.

clue.text: Upset as tree is put in another position

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tree is uprooted and replanted somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of AS TREE gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal: to reseat something is to seat it again, setting it in a new place.

clue.text: Capital a judge has visited in the past when retired

indicators.note: the letters for a judge pay a visit inside the reversed piece
retired means withdrawn, going backwards, so the run is reversed

parts.note: something in the past is over, finished
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A city that a magistrate visited long ago once he had stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns the pair round to SAREVO; 'has visited' sets A J within it. 'retired' looks like the judge stopping work. Sarajevo is the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper-name example: the city is the seat of government of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

clue.text: Possibly cut risk with a rest at the end, it's assumed, if exercising

indicators.note: possibly says the letters might take another form, so they are rearranged
at the end picks the final letter of rest

explanation.surface: Maybe you could reduce danger by resting after the workout.
explanation.walkthrough: CUT RISK and A rearranged give TRACKSUI; T, the last letter of rest, completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: a garment one assumes, that is puts on, for exercise or training.

clue.text: Answer given by King facing gutless popish plot

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is King George's cipher

indicators.note: gutless means the insides are taken out, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: A monarch's reply to a hollow Catholic conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' suggests a conspiracy after 'popish' (the Popish Plot of 1678), but it is a chart. 'gutless' leaves P and H of popish.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to plot points is to draw them on a chart, and a graph is that chart.

clue.text: Duck behind deer every now and again

indicators.note: every now and again picks letters at intervals, the even ones here

explanation.surface: A waterbird following a deer from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth, sixth and so on letters of BEHIND DEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the eider is a large sea duck, prized for its down.

clue.text: German writer, like an ass, ignoring European fashion model

parts.note: Thomas Mann was a German novelist

indicators.note: ignoring means one letter of the equine word is left out

parts.note: an ass is in the horse family, so like an ass is equine

explanation.surface: A German author, foolish as a donkey, has no time for continental style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like an ass' sounds like an insult but means horse-like, EQUINE; 'ignoring' drops one E.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a mannequin is a dummy, or a person, used to display clothes.

clue.text: Take advantage of tolerance shown by cricket side

parts.note: play is the slack or freedom of movement in a mechanism, its tolerance
the on side is the half of a cricket field behind the batsman's legs

explanation.surface: Exploit the leniency shown by a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to play on someone's fears is to exploit them for gain.

clue.text: Try to obtain negative vote over multiple bets

indicators.note: over signals that the joined pieces are turned around

parts.note: to seek is to try to obtain
a nay is a vote against

explanation.surface: Attempt to secure a 'no' vote on a whole series of wagers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses SEEK NAY. A Yankee is a British bet of eleven wagers on four selections.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yankee combines doubles, trebles and an accumulator on four horses, so it is a multiple bet.

clue.text: Female band leader muttered about including one sort of key

indicators.note: including means the rearranged letters hold the next piece
about means the letters move around into a new order

parts.note: a major key is one kind of musical key

explanation.surface: A woman leading a marching band grumbled about a musical key.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters give DRUMETTE, and 'including' sets the key's name in after the first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum majorette is a girl who leads or marches with a band, twirling a baton.

clue.text: Disappointment lowered or lengthened

definitions.meaning: a disappointment is an anticlimax, a failure to meet hopes
lowered means brought down, as on a rope
lengthened, of a hem or trousers, means having the fold undone to make them longer

explanation.surface: A letdown: lowered, or else made longer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a disappointment as a noun, and as a verb past participle both lowered and a lengthened hem.

clue.text: My way to stop cunning plan quietly dismissed

indicators.note: to stop means to plug, so the abbreviation for way fills a gap inside
dismissed means sent away, so the letter for quietly goes

parts.note: a ploy is a cunning plan
P, piano, means quietly in music
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Here is the speaker's method to block a crafty scheme that was silently dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks possessive but is an exclamation of surprise. 'dismissed' leaves LOY, and 'to stop' plugs the road abbreviation into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise, like 'goodness me'.

clue.text: Regan distressed in drama being shown up as sycophant

indicators.note: in places the rearranged name inside the reversed word for drama
shown up in a down clue means read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: Noh is a classical Japanese drama

indicators.note: distressed means upset and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Regan, troubled in a play, is exposed as a flatterer.
explanation.walkthrough: Regan is a scheming daughter in King Lear. Her name rearranged sits inside HON, the Japanese drama turned upwards by 'being shown up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a hanger-on is a parasitic follower who flatters for favour.

clue.text: Plain exercise ending part of dance

indicators.note: ending means the exercise letters come at the end of the dance piece

parts.note: a step is a movement in a dance
PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: Gym workout finishing off one bit of a dance routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective for the exercise, but it is the noun for flat grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A steppe is a vast treeless grassy plain, as in Russia and Central Asia.

clue.text: Country rating an "E" after turmoil …

indicators.note: after turmoil means the letters come out once thrown into confusion, rearranged

explanation.surface: A nation given a poor E grade after unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: RATING AN E rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper-name example: Argentina is a South American country.

clue.text: … a distant country briefly featured in thin buff periodical?

indicators.note: featured in means placed inside the word for thin

parts.note: fine can mean thin, as in fine thread
NZ is short for New Zealand, a far-off country

explanation.surface: Following the previous clue, a far land appears in a slim magazine for enthusiasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thin buff' reads as a colour, but thin is FINE and buff begins the definition: a fan's magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanzine is a magazine produced by enthusiasts, or buffs, for others; the question mark marks the play.

clue.text: Endearments from fools impressing somebody without importance

indicators.note: impressing means pressing in, so the plural for fools holds the next piece

parts.note: a fool is a fruit dessert, so fools are sweets
an insignificant person is a nothing

explanation.surface: Pet names from idiots who impress an insignificant person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fools' look like idiots, but a fool is a creamy British fruit pudding, so fools are SWEETS (desserts).
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: words of affection whispered between lovers are endearments.

clue.text: Start to talk extremely animatedly about cyberpunk writer

indicators.note: start to talk means the first letter of talk

parts.note: a cyberpunk can be a computer hacker

indicators.note: extremely picks the two extreme letters of animatedly

explanation.surface: Begin chatting very excitedly about a science-fiction author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cyberpunk writer' looks like one phrase, but the definition is just 'writer'. 'about' puts HACKER inside A and Y, the ends of animatedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper-name example: William Makepeace Thackeray wrote Vanity Fair.

clue.text: Need just revealed in a provocative way

parts.note: a need is a want
just means only, as in 'just one'

explanation.surface: Desire alone is shown in a seductive manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealed' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wantonly means in an unrestrained or sexually provocative manner.

clue.text: What may be afoot lands Conservative in disgrace

indicators.note: lands means sets down, so the letter for Conservative is landed within the footwear

parts.note: a sandal is worn on a foot, so it may be a-foot

explanation.surface: Some event in progress puts a Tory in shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afoot' means happening, but read as 'a foot', and what may be on one is a SANDAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a scandal is a public disgrace caused by wrongdoing.

clue.text: Removal of monarch — troops securing country after uprising

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a monarch

indicators.note: after uprising means the word for country is read upwards, reversed in a down clue

parts.note: USA is a country
RE, the Royal Engineers, are troops

explanation.surface: Deposing a king or queen as the army holds a land after revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' suggests a revolt, but it turns USA into ASU; 'securing' is a link with RE (Royal Engineers) holding the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an erasure is a removal, the act of rubbing something out.

clue.text: Gather there's a problem on the day

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
MON is short for Monday, a day

explanation.surface: Collect yourself: something is wrong today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's' and 'on' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to summon people is to call them together, to gather them.

clue.text: Pick up good tip

parts.note: to tip is to lean, slant

explanation.surface: Get a useful bit of advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' looks like a piece of advice, but it is the verb meaning slant.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to glean information is to pick it up bit by bit.
